entries.title: nightly cycle repairs yfinance's cache and catches up each ticker on its own
entries.body: yfinance's ticker time-zone cache (py-yfinance/tkr-tz.db) was corrupt on 30 October, so every index lookup failed with "database disk image is malformed", and one exception stopped the whole pre-publish catch-up. The daily cycle now checks yfinance's caches first and removes a damaged one (yfinance rebuilds it), and the catch-up handles each ticker separately and logs any that fail.

entries.title: stand-in daily bar from 15-minute bars when Yahoo posts the stock's bar late
entries.body: On 29 and 30 October Yahoo posted the deep-tier stocks' daily bars between 20:50 and 21:00 New York, after the nightly cycle had looked twice, while the index bars and the stocks' 15-minute bars were already there. Before publishing, a ticker still missing the latest complete session now gets that day's bar from its 15-minute bars (open, high, low, close, volume; adj_close = close). The next run re-fetches the last week and Yahoo's official bar overwrites it; the split check ignores the latest stored bar, so the closing-auction difference doesn't force a re-download. This runs after the paper bot, which keeps trading official bars only.

entries.title: give the quantum simulations 20 minutes before keeping yesterday's results
entries.body: They take about 2.5 minutes on an idle PC, but on 29 October the laptop ran on battery and they took over 8 minutes, so the 5-minute limit kept the 27 October results and the Quantum page stayed amber. The publish waits for them either way; a longer limit only matters on a slow night.

entries.title: nightly publish works under the scheduled task; re-check daily bars before publishing
entries.body: The 29 October nightly run refreshed every source but didn't publish: the publish gate (calculation tests) ran under pythonw, which has no console handles, and the Node.js tests failed with OSError WinError 50. The gate now gives its test run stdin=DEVNULL. Yahoo also posted the 28 October daily bars for the indices but not yet for the deep-tier stocks when the cycle ran, so the stock pages showed the 27th: the cycle now fetches those daily bars once more after the ~40-minute universe refresh, just before publishing. Tests cover both.

entries.title: lint passes on committed code; underlined credits link; 24px methodology links
entries.body: ruff flagged an unused import already committed in quant/trading_bot.py, which has uncommitted work in progress elsewhere, so it is ignored for that file only until that work lands. Lighthouse on the live site flagged the new credits link on the about page (link distinguished by colour alone) and the methodology contents links (under 24 px tall); both fixed.

entries.title: unique title and description per route, static entry pages, sitemap and a favicon set
entries.body: Each route sets its own document title and meta description (English and Korean). The export writes /global/, /markets/, ... entry pages with their own title, description, Open Graph tags and canonical URL, plus sitemap.xml and robots.txt. A favicon set (ico, svg, png, apple-touch, web manifest) replaces the inline data-URI icon, and Plotly toolbar links get role=button.

entries.title: loading, empty and error states with a retry button on every panel
entries.body: errorBox(message, retry) shows the reason and a "Try again" button that re-runs just that panel (or the page). Failed downloads aren't cached, so a retry really fetches again. Used by: - every price chart (Markets, both Stock pages, the drawer), the factor   model, Compare and its correlation panel, the risk and portfolio labs,   the Live chart and the Finnhub lookups; - the page-level "Data not available" screen; - the chart library itself if it can't load. Price failures now say the price service couldn't be reached instead of the browser's "Failed to fetch". Panels that wait show a loading line (the watchlist panel did not), and empty panels say why they're empty.

entries.title: every page usable at 375px; heatmaps become ranked lists on phones
entries.body: - The sector heatmap shows a ranked list (name, signed move, a bar for   its size) below 640px, with a Map / List switch at any width; the   correlation heatmap shows every pair ranked, keeping the matrix for   screen readers. - Tables already scroll inside their own frame; grid columns no longer   stretch to fit a wide table, the Global tabs scroll, sparklines and   formulas fit the screen, and filters stack full-width. - Checked at 375px on every route: nothing runs past the screen edge.

entries.title: hand-checked tests for every financial calculation; publish blocked on failure
entries.body: tests/test_calculations.py checks each calculation against small inputs worked out by hand in the comments: - returns (daily, since a date, annualised), volatility, max drawdown,   Sharpe, Sortino, beta and the risk-free adjustment; - factor regression on an exactly known stock, correlation, VaR and   CVaR, and Black-Scholes (textbook and Hull 15.6 values, put-call   parity); - the qubit simulator and Grover probabilities; - the Python versions: series metrics, performance stats, the factor   model and market regimes.

entries.title: Korean / English toggle covering every page, with the dictionary in one file
entries.body: A 한국어 / English button in the header of every page switches the language and is remembered in localStorage; a Korean browser starts in Korean. The pages stay written in English, and docs/assets/i18n.js translates the interface as it draws from docs/assets/i18n.ko.js (about 1,800 entries keyed by the English): - Numbers, dates and tickers become placeholders, so one entry covers   every value; dates and dollar amounts are written the Korean way. - Inline links and bold become slots, so Korean word order works. - The scorer's reasons are translated clause by clause; chart labels,   toasts and alerts use the same dictionary. - Tickers, company names, headlines, commit messages and formulas are   data and stay as they are; methodology, glossary, About and Privacy   are translated. Text with no entry stays English and is listed by I18N.report() or #...?i18n=missing; a tour of every page in Korean found none left.

entries.title: feedback through GitHub Issues, with bug, data-error and feature forms
entries.body: Three issue forms ask for what each kind of report needs. All three ask what you'd like to see changed; bugs and data errors also ask for the page's shareable link, and data errors add the ticker, the metric and its as-of date. config.yml points security reports to the private channel in SECURITY.md and questions to the Methodology page. Every footer and the Start page link to "Suggest a feature / report a bug". A data-check note opens the data-error form with its link pre-filled.

entries.title: PNG export for every chart, watermarked with the site and as-of date
entries.body: Every Plotly chart gets a PNG button next to CSV. The chart is rendered client-side (Plotly.toImage) onto a canvas with a footer strip: the panel's title on the left, the site's address and the data's as-of date (from the panel's freshness badge) on the right. The address is also printed faintly in the top corner. The Live chart's screenshot button uses the same watermark with the latest bar's time.

entries.title: daily brief on Global, written by the nightly job, last 30 archived
entries.body: quant/web/brief.py writes a few sentences by rule from tonight's data, in English and Korean, with no AI: - the five largest moves among stocks worth $10B or more; - the best and worst sector, cap-weighted; - factor ETFs (MTUM, VLUE, QUAL, USMV, IWM) against SPY, notable at a   0.5 pp gap or more; - the VIX change, and the 10-year and 2-year Treasury yields from FRED. A rule that fails or has no data is skipped, not fatal. Each night's brief is kept in data/briefs and the latest 30 are published; Global shows the date and an archive picker whose choice is part of the link.

entries.title: Start here page (#/start), where first-time visitors land
entries.body: Three guided examples, each one click, open their page with everything filled in through the shareable-link state: - Samsung Electronics against SK hynix, TSMC, Apple and Nvidia on   Compare; - a five-stock $10,000 basket in the VaR / CVaR risk lab; - a 90-day Apple call priced by Black-Scholes, Monte Carlo and the   nightly quantum run. A visit with no address and no "visited" flag in localStorage goes here; later visits start on Global. Start is first in the menu.

entries.title: shareable links for every view, a Copy link button and link previews
entries.body: Each page writes its state after the hash route, so a copied link reproduces the view in a fresh browser: - Global: filters, sort, page, tab and sector drill-down. - Markets: range, news scope and indicators. - Stock: range, annotations and indicators. Financials: model. - Compare: tickers, window, model and correlation settings. - Quantum: the option, risk and portfolio labs, including baskets and   weights. - Live: interval and chart type. Every value is checked before use. A header button copies the link. Open Graph and Twitter tags point to a 1200x630 PNG preview, so links unfurl in KakaoTalk, Slack and Discord.

entries.title: watchlist stars everywhere, panels on Global and Live, JSON export/import
entries.body: One star button and one click handler serve every ticker: the screener, peers, Compare's columns and the Live chart's title. A watchlist card on Global and Live lists each name with its 1-day move. It exports the list as JSON and imports a file back, merging it and skipping anything that isn't a ticker. The list stays in localStorage behind try/catch.

entries.title: red notice when the factor file is missing; pretty links for the new pages
entries.body: Financials' factor model now says which data file is missing, with a red badge, instead of a bare error. 404.html also redirects /status, /track-record and /changelog to their hash routes.

entries.title: one disclaimer block, word for word, on every page and in every CSV
entries.body: "Research and education only, not investment advice. Data may be delayed or wrong. Past performance does not predict future results." now sits in the footer of every page (index, About, Privacy, 404) and heads every CSV download. The scattered variants in captions are gone, and a test keeps it that way.

entries.title: "View the code" link and a README section on verifying a number
entries.body: The header and footer of every page link to the repository as "View the code". The README's new "How to verify a number" walks through the freshness badge, the Data status page, the Methodology entry, the CSV downloads, rebuilding the export, the append-only track record and the changelog.

entries.title: changelog page generated from feat/fix commits (#/changelog)
entries.body: The export reads the git history and publishes changelog.json with every commit whose subject starts with feat: or fix: (Conventional Commits, optional scope). Commits scoped "methodology", or touching a file that defines a calculation, are marked and listed first. When git isn't available the last good changelog is republished.

entries.title: CSV download on every table and chart
entries.body: A small CSV button sits above every table, Plotly chart and data panel (FRED tiles, sector map, the Live chart's bars). Each file starts with the panel's title, its sources with their as-of dates (taken from the panel's freshness badge), the download time and page, and the disclaimer. The screener's file holds every matching row, not just the visible page.

entries.title: append-only signal log and a track-record page (#/track-record)
entries.body: Each night the export appends that night's BUY / HOLD / AVOID labels to data/track: one file per signal date, created in exclusive mode, plus a manifest line holding the file's SHA-256 and the previous line's hash. A rerun for a logged date, or an older date, changes nothing, so the log is never rewritten or backfilled. The page shows forward returns after 5, 20 and 60 trading days against each market's index, the hit rate, the number of signal dates and the start date, and labels any row with fewer than 60 observations. The latest days' signals are downloadable without prices.

entries.title: freshness badge on every panel
entries.body: Each panel heading names its source and as-of date in a badge that links to Data status. Colour follows status.json's rule, recomputed in the visitor's browser: green, amber once the data is older than the source's expected age (one trading day for prices), red when it is missing, failed or more than three times too old. Prices loaded in the browser use their last bar's date; a failed load shows red. Headings a view doesn't label itself get the page's main source, and text-only sections opt out.

entries.title: status.json from the nightly job and a Data status page (#/status)
entries.body: The export now runs every step fail-soft and writes status.json: per source the last successful run, data date, row counts, missing tickers, stale series, outliers beyond 5 standard deviations and the quality checks. A missing file or a failed step turns its sources red instead of stopping the run. Symbols that fail a check carry a mark in the screener and a note on their pages; a missing data file shows a red notice, not a partial page. The footer links to the new page.

entries.title: fail-soft data-quality checks for the nightly job
entries.body: quant/web/quality.py checks a wide price table for repeated dates or symbols, gaps of 3+ sessions between two prices, closes at or below zero, zero volume on 5+ of the last 20 sessions and one-day jumps of 20x either way (a unit change such as pence to pounds). It also lists stale series and daily moves beyond 5 standard deviations for review. A check that raises is recorded with its error and the others still run; the results feed status.json and per-symbol flags.

rule: Commits tagged feat: or fix: (Conventional Commits). Methodology changes are highlighted.
